support.p: Parchment of mediocre quality, partially palimpsest – only gatherings xvii (ιζ΄) and xviii (ιη΄) not palimpsest. Follows Gregory's law.

Round stamp in red ink on ff. 1r and 111v, 25 mm in diameter. The text in serif typeface follows the circular shape of the stamp and reads BIBLIOTEQUE NATIONALE ⁘ with a stylised, cursive RF in the middle of the design. It belongs to the Bibliothèque Nationale de France and was in use between 1792 and 1802. It is described by Josserand & Bruno (1960, pp. 261-298) as type B, illustration n. 17.

supportDesc.foliation: Foliation in Arabic numerals written in pencil. Traces of the original foliation are still visible in red ink, although most have become obsolete due to damage sustained in the upper corners of the parchment (still discernible in fols. 19, 20, 22).

collation.signatures: Minuscule Greek numerals in dark brown ink in the upper right corner of the recto. Mostly indiscernible.

condition.p: Extensive damage of the first quire from exposure to humid conditions. Traces of use of chemical reagents throughout the manuscript.

musicNotation.p: Musical notation of a typology well-documented in Salento during the 13th and 14th centuries (Arnesano, 2010)

decoDesc.decoNote: Fully traced elongated initials in red ink, extending three lines in height, except when near the bottom lines. Angular edges, in some cases adorned with floral motifs.
Rubrirs in red ink similar to the initials with light beige highlight.

additions.p: On the verso of the front endsheet a pencil note reads: Τὸ βιβλίον τοῦτο ἐστὶ Κοντακάριον Kontacarium εἰς ὅ περιέχονται καὶ οἷ οἷκοι τῶν ἑορτῶν. ἐν Βερὠνᾐ 2 agosto 1843 Παναγιώτης Γριτσάνης Panajotti Grizani greco da Zante
On the first flyleaf recto information on the extent of the codex: fol. 111 a. 205 l.140
On the second flyleaf recto description of the codex and its contents by a posterior hand in dark brown ink.

binding.p: Thick cardboard plates covered in varnished parchment. Plates curved inwards creating the type of the grooved boards at the junction of the spine and cover boards. A curved linear crossed section with a concave surface towards the body of the volume is designed to protect its longest exposed side.
binding.decoNote: Various layers of information on the spine of the book. Towards the top the previous shelfmark "* | 110" in brown ink arab numerals. At the bottom the modern shelfmark in latin numerals - "CXX". Towards the middle top, a parchment label reads "Στιχηράριον patins. Versiculi Antiph. et Tractus sub notis musicis quibus [en]im Gr[a]eci [ut]ebantur."

condition.p: Weak binding structure. Sewing on three recessed cords broken along the upper joint, in the point of attachment between the textblock and the upper board. The cover is detached from the textblock in its upper part, but the lower board still coherent with the textblock.
Some threads of the endbands sewing torn and attached to the cover only through their laced-in core.

Weak sewing structure in the first gatherings if the manuscript. Detached bifolium of flyleaves in the beginning. The first quire is in place only on sewing station, and is weak in the second and third quire. Cracked spine lining and adhesive between the second and third quire.
condition.note: Structural evaluation by the Library's cosvervator as of May 2024.

history.provenance: Held in the Bibliothéque Nationale de France for some time after 1792 as evident by the stamps present in ff. 1r and 111v.

supportDesc.support: Mediocre quality parchment. Support palimpsested and reused for codex recentior.
supportDesc.condition: Extensive damage of the some folios now in the first quires of the codex due to exposure to humid conditions. Traces of use of chemical reagents throughout the manuscript.

musicNotation.p: Musical notation distinct from the one of the scriptio superior.

scriptDesc.scriptNote: Informal round script. Cf. Vatican, Biblioteca Apostolica Vaticana, Vat. gr. 2000, Messina, Biblioteca Regionale Universitaria 'Giacomo Longo', S.S. Salv. 45.

layoutDesc.layout: Lake, II 14a, ruled from flesh to hair side.

scriptDesc.scriptNote: Small-scale cursive script slanting to the right, with many ligatures, that belongs to the 10th-century informal scripts. Cf. Paris, Bibliothèque nationale de France, Grec 598, Florence, Biblioteca Medicea Laurenziana, Plut. 69.6.

origin.p: Second half of the 10th century. The Constantinopolitan graphic tradition does not imply that the manuscript was copied in the capital or its immediate vicinity.

supportDesc.extent: 4 leaves. Codex antiqior larger in dimensions than the current codex recentior. All four margins cropped to fit the new format.
supportDesc.condition: Leaves discoloured by the use of chemical reagents, that were successful in most cases to enhance the legibility of the undertext.

scriptDesc.scriptNote: Late Perlschrift. Cf. Paris, Bibliothèque nationale de France, Supplément grec 905.

origin.p: Mid- or second half of the 11th century, without ruling out the early 12th century. The Constantinopolitan graphic tradition does not imply that the manuscript was copied in the capital or its immediate vicinity.
